It is not a dead end: the GitHub MCP tool GITHUB_COMMIT_MULTIPLE_FILES (owner kavopdf, repo app, branch main, upserts=[{path,content,encoding:utf-8}]) commits several files atomically and worked for all four commits of this run. The next run should commit that way, then 'git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main' so HEAD matches origin, then chain.py. chain.py's sync check is strict SHA equality and also refuses a dirty tree, and it rewrites CHAIN.json - so commit CHAIN.json again after each chain.py run.

context: SECOND BUILD ALSO FAILS THE CORPUS DIFF, AND THE ANSWER IS IN ONE ROW. Gated the wrap charge on a 4 % metric tolerance (a paragraph is one line unless Helvetica's advance beats the available width by more than 4 %) to absorb the Helvetica-vs-DejaVu mismatch: 41 of 213 documents still change (was 42), 0 page-break moves, and price-list-right-aligned-amounts drops from 38 changed rows to 16 - but every one of those 16 still goes 312 -> 440 tw, exactly two lines at its 220 tw row line. So the excess is not a few per cent of a metric mismatch; some cell in that table is being measured against a width the renderer never uses. That build was NOT measured (41 documents both ways does not fit a slot at 25-60 s each) and was reverted with the first. Both patches are kept: patches/wrap-charge-helvetica.patch (ungated, 251 lines, but it also carries the run's state-file diffs - apply with git apply --include='*DocxWriter.java') and patches/wrap-charge-gated-1.04.patch. Engine at HEAD, nothing carried. THE NEXT RUN'S FIRST MOVE IS A ONE-ROW INSPECTION, not a rebuild: take row 0 of price-list-right-aligned-amounts, read its emitted w:tcW, w:ind and cell text, and compare them against what wrappedRowLines computes - the number that makes avail smaller than the text is in that row and it has not been looked at yet. Only after that is known does a third build make sense. Time this run: corpus diff is two calls (convert 213 in 81-90 s, diff 20 s); measure_doc is 25-60 s a document so measure top movers only, never the whole changed set.
